name: CyberAv3ngers
summary: An IRGC-affiliated threat persona associated with disruptive targeting of exposed operational technology, most visibly the 2023 Unitronics PLC/HMI campaign.
primaryFocus: Internet-exposed operational technology and critical infrastructure

stateAffiliation.assessment: U.S. government reporting attributes the Unitronics activity to IRGC-affiliated actors using the CyberAv3ngers persona; MITRE records the group as suspected IRGC-affiliated.

observedSince.label: CyberAv3ngers persona
observedSince.qualification: MITRE reports activity since at least 2020.

observedSince.label: Global Unitronics campaign
observedSince.qualification: Government reporting documents global PLC/HMI targeting beginning in November 2023.

designations.name: CyberAv3ngers
designations.description: MITRE's group record for the persona and its Unitronics defacement campaign.

designations.name: IRGC-affiliated cyber actors using the CyberAv3ngers persona
designations.description: Government attribution scope for the actors responsible for the Unitronics targeting.

designations.name: BAUXITE
designations.description: Dragos reports substantial technical overlap; BAUXITE remains a separate vendor-defined activity cluster.

designations.name: Soldiers of Solomon
designations.description: Reported as connected to CyberAv3ngers, not treated as a proven alias.

assessment.text: CyberAv3ngers achieved operational disruption through low-complexity access paths: exposed Unitronics controllers, default or absent credentials, replacement of ladder logic and defacement of HMI displays.
The persona has mixed verified intrusions with disputed or false claims of Israeli critical-infrastructure compromise, so public claims require independent technical corroboration.
IOCONTROL expands the overlap activity from opportunistic PLC defacement to persistent Linux access across OT and IoT device families, but the malware itself contains no ICS-specific process logic.

campaigns.name: Unitronics defacement campaign
campaigns.summary: IRGC-affiliated actors accessed internet-facing Unitronics PLC/HMI devices using default or absent passwords, replaced ladder logic and changed operator displays.
campaigns.impact: At least 75 U.S. devices were affected, including at least 34 water and wastewater facilities; consequences included loss of view, availability and normal operation.

campaigns.name: Disputed Israeli infrastructure claims
campaigns.summary: The group has publicized claims of critical-infrastructure compromise in Israel, some of which government reporting describes as false or disputed.
campaigns.impact: Information effects can exaggerate technical reach and complicate attribution and incident validation.

campaigns.name: IOCONTROL deployment
campaigns.summary: Custom Linux payloads established MQTT-based remote access across multiple OT and IoT device families.
campaigns.impact: Persistent command execution and potential lateral movement from embedded devices; no ICS-specific process capability was identified in the malware.

capabilities.name: Access exposed PLC/HMI devices
capabilities.description: Authenticate to publicly reachable Unitronics devices through default or absent credentials.

capabilities.name: Replace ladder logic and operator graphics
capabilities.description: Erase original logic, download actor-controlled logic and replace the HMI display.

capabilities.name: Maintain Linux device access
capabilities.description: Deploy IOCONTROL for remote command execution and persistence over encrypted MQTT communications.

malware.name: IOCONTROL
malware.description: A device-specific Linux backdoor using MQTT over TCP 8883 for command and control; public analysis found no ICS-specific logic.

enterprise.name: Brute Force
enterprise.behaviour: Actors attempted password access against exposed devices and services.

enterprise.name: Valid Accounts: Default Accounts
enterprise.behaviour: Default Unitronics password 1111 and absent authentication enabled access.

enterprise.name: Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
enterprise.behaviour: The actors replaced ladder logic and HMI content stored on affected controllers.

ics.name: Internet Accessible Device
ics.behaviour: Publicly reachable Unitronics PLC/HMI devices and cellular equipment were targeted.

ics.name: Insecure Credentials: Default Credentials
ics.behaviour: Factory-set credentials were used to access exposed controllers.

ics.name: Denial of Service
ics.behaviour: Controller defacement and communication failure prevented normal device operation.

ics.name: Loss of Availability
ics.behaviour: Affected organisations halted operations when PLC/HMI functions became unavailable.

ics.name: Loss of Productivity and Revenue
ics.behaviour: Industrial disruption interfered with normal business operations.

ics.name: Loss of View
ics.behaviour: Replacement graphics prevented operators from viewing PLC information on the HMI.

indicatorNotice: Indicators associated with the 2024 IOCONTROL reporting are historical and may now be reassigned, sinkholed or benign. Use them only with source date, enrichment and behavioural context.

defensivePriorities.name: Remove direct internet exposure
defensivePriorities.description: Inventory and isolate internet-reachable PLCs, HMIs, cellular gateways and embedded management interfaces.

defensivePriorities.name: Eliminate default credentials
defensivePriorities.description: Change factory passwords, require strong unique authentication and verify every Unitronics deployment.

defensivePriorities.name: Monitor logic and HMI integrity
defensivePriorities.description: Alert on unauthorised downloads, graphic changes, configuration drift and unexpected controller restarts.

defensivePriorities.name: Hunt the IOCONTROL behaviour
defensivePriorities.description: Prioritise unexpected MQTT 8883, DoH resolution, new startup scripts and binaries on embedded Linux devices over historical indicator-only matches.
